skill.name: teach
skill.description: Build a teaching workspace that adapts lessons, resources, records, and reference material to the user's learning goal.

content.value_statement: Learning over multiple sessions often loses context and repeats old material. This skill creates a workspace of missions, lessons, records, resources, and references.
actual_capabilities: Creates a mission document that ties learning to a concrete goal.
Curates trusted resources and community references for future lessons.
Produces short HTML lessons with citations and practice activities.
Maintains learning records to track prior knowledge and misconceptions.
Builds reusable lesson assets and reference documents inside the workspace.
Uses glossary guidance to keep terminology consistent across sessions.
limitations: The skill depends on accurate user goals and honest progress signals.
It does not replace expert instruction for regulated or safety-critical topics.
External resource quality depends on the agent tools available during use.
It creates workspace files, so users should review generated lesson content.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Learning Path
use_cases.description: Turn a broad topic into a concrete mission, first lesson, and source list.

use_cases.title: Teach Technical Concepts
use_cases.description: Create focused lessons, references, and records for a programming topic.

use_cases.title: Support Team Upskilling
use_cases.description: Build reusable lesson materials that keep shared terminology and progress visible.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Topic
prompt_templates.prompt: Teach me the basics of TypeScript generics. Help me define my mission first.

prompt_templates.title: Create the First Lesson
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my mission and resources to create a short first lesson with one practice activity.

prompt_templates.title: Continue From Records
prompt_templates.prompt: Read my learning records and teach the next concept that fits my current level.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Reference System
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a concise reference document and update the glossary from the last lesson.

output_examples.input: Teach me Rust for building a command line tool.
output_examples.output: A mission statement, a curated resource list, and a first lesson about ownership basics.

output_examples.input: Continue my strength training course from the last session.
output_examples.output: A lesson matched to prior records, a short practice task, and one new learning record.

output_examples.input: Help my team learn incident review writing.
output_examples.output: A focused lesson, shared terminology, and reusable reference notes for future reviews.

best_practices: Start with a specific mission before asking for lessons.
Keep resources curated, annotated, and tied to the mission.
Review learning records before each new session.
anti_patterns: Do not use one workspace for unrelated learning goals.
Do not accept lessons without checking cited sources.
Do not create long lessons that exceed the user's current level.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates mission notes, resource lists, HTML lessons, learning records, references, assets, and glossary guidance.

faq.question: Does it work across sessions?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses workspace files to remember goals, prior knowledge, and useful resources.

faq.question: Can it teach non-coding topics?
faq.answer: Yes. The format supports programming, fitness, writing, process skills, and other structured topics.

faq.question: Does it browse the web automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can recommend resource gathering, but browsing depends on the host agent and user permission.

faq.question: Is it a full learning management system?
faq.answer: No. It is a workspace pattern for personalized lessons and records.

faq.question: Should users review generated lessons?
faq.answer: Yes. Users should check facts, citations, and any generated files before relying on them.
